title: Balinese water temples help organise a shared irrigation system
body: Bali's subak system, which dates to the ninth century, coordinates water for rice farms through canals and weirs. Water temples are focal points in this cooperative management system.
takeaway: A working water network needs an agreement about sharing the flow as well as channels that carry it.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Cultural Landscape of Bali Province (2012)
visual: a small water temple above stepped Balinese rice fields

title: The UN counted 33 megacities in 2025, up from eight in 1975
body: Under the UN's 2025 definition, a megacity is an urban area with at least 10 million people. The count rose from eight in 1975 to 33 in 2025 using a consistent definition across countries.
takeaway: The result depends on where the urban area ends, so a municipal population alone can miss the size of a city.
visual: an immense city skyline extending across a broad plain

title: Rural workers earned less per hour in a study of 58 countries
body: An International Labour Organization study published in 2024 compared rural and urban workers across 58 countries. Rural workers earned about 24% less per hour on average. Differences in education, experience and occupation explained roughly half the gap.
takeaway: Where people work can mark a difference in earnings that comparing job titles alone will miss.
source: Ananian and Dellaferrera, International Labour Organization Working Paper 107 (2024)
visual: a rural workshop at the edge of a road leading towards a distant city
